naslov: Gateway to Kopački rit – a trip through Bilje Municipality

koraci.tekst: Eight villages on about 260 km² between the Drava and the Danube. Almost the whole eastern part of the municipality is Kopački rit Nature Park – one of the largest preserved floodplains in Europe. The municipal office and the tourist board are in the centre of Bilje.

Kopački rit is on the Ramsar list of wetlands of international importance and part of the UNESCO transboundary Mura–Drava–Danube Biosphere Reserve. The map shows the core area, buffer zone and transition area in which we live and work.

The Mali Sakadaš visitor centre near Kopačevo has a multimedia exhibition; next to it are the horse-powered mill (suvara) and the white water-lily boardwalk. Boat trips through the wetland start from the Veliki Sakadaš landing.

The Mali Sakadaš, Veliki Sakadaš and Podunavlje fishponds trails lead through forests, ponds and along canals. Boards along the way introduce the fish and birds of the wetland – spring and autumn migration are the best times for birdwatching.
In the forest in the north of the park lies the Tikveš castle complex with the New Castle, a country villa, a visitor centre and an educational trail. The complex is a protected cultural asset.

Protected and listed buildings stand in every village, from Bilje and Kopačevo to Zlatna Greda, and archaeological sites lie under the fields – including the Roman road near Bilje and sites near Kopačevo and Vardarac.
The Pannonian Peace Route, the Danube Route and Baranja Greenways cross the municipality. A cycle and footpath links Bilje with Osijek, and new sections are being built.
The Podunavlje canals, the Čarna and the Grabovac lakes are popular fishing spots. Special rules and permits of the Kopački rit Nature Park apply inside the park.
Viewpoints from the landscape study show where the finest views over the wetland, fields and villages are – ideal for photographers and evening walks.
Restaurants in Bilje, Kopačevo and Tikveš serve local cuisine – fish dishes and game for which Baranja is known.
Fields, ponds and river arms carry old names that are slowly being forgotten. Explore the official names and add your own old photo or story.
Check the weather before your trip; bus stops are on the map. Enjoy your stay in Bilje!
